headline: Domain-fueled growth swings CoStar back to profit

kpis.label: Operating income
kpis.delta: n/m (prior-year quarter was a $27M operating loss)

summary_short: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 rose 18.4% y/y to $925M, led by Residential Real Estate (+33% to $444M, including $70M from the Domain acquisition) and Commercial Real Estate (+8% to $481M); net income swung to $55M from $6M as operating income moved from a $27M loss to a $76M profit.
summary_long: Revenue rose 18.4% y/y to $925M: Commercial Real Estate (+8% to $481M) gained from CoStar subscriber growth and LoopNet listings, while Residential Real Estate rose 33% to $444M on $70M of Domain-acquisition revenue plus more Apartments.com/Homes.com memberships. Gross margin ticked up to 78.7% from 78.5%. Operating income swung to $76M from a $27M loss as revenue growth outpaced a 2% rise in opex, helped by a Brown Judgment litigation recovery in G&A. Net income rose to $55M from $6M; diluted EPS rose to $0.14 from $0.01. Cash was $1.27B, down sharply y/y after 2025's Domain/Matterport cash deals and $589M of 2026 buybacks. CoStar agreed in May 2026 to buy Zonda for ~$800M cash, closing expected H2 2026.

drivers.explanation: Commercial Real Estate +8% ($481M) on CoStar subscriber growth, price increases, and STR Benchmarking sales, plus LoopNet listings growth; Residential Real Estate +33% ($444M) on $70M of Domain-acquisition revenue and more Apartments.com/Homes.com memberships.

Margin rose to 79% from 78% as revenue growth outpaced a 17% rise in cost of revenue, which included higher Matterport/Domain intangible amortization and Domain web-hosting, data, and personnel costs.
Higher amortization from the Matterport and Domain acquisitions plus Domain web-hosting, data, and personnel costs, partially offset by a $2M gain on the sale of the research plane.
Swung to a $76M profit from a $27M loss because 18% revenue growth far outpaced a 2% rise in total operating expenses, aided by a G&A gain from Brown Judgment litigation recoveries.
Tracks the operating-income swing plus a shift to $2M of net interest expense (including $9M of Brown Judgment-related interest) from $33M of net interest income a year ago; tax expense rose to $19M.
Tracks the net-income swing; weighted diluted share count also fell 4.7% y/y on buybacks, a modest additional per-share lift.

Rose modestly q/q as $267M of YTD operating cash flow outpaced $110M of investing outflows; the much larger y/y decline instead reflects 2025's Domain/Matterport cash acquisitions and buybacks, not this quarter.
Declined y/y as $589M of year-to-date 2026 share buybacks under the $1.5B Stock Repurchase Program, including a $500M ASR completed in March 2026, outpaced retained net income.
Fell y/y as the company repurchased 13.8 million shares for $589 million year-to-date under its Stock Repurchase Program, including an ASR completed in March 2026.
Fell to 26% of pretax income from 73% a year earlier; the filing attributes the change in tax expense to higher pretax income and does not further explain the swing in rate.

The filing frames the quarter as revenue growth (Domain, CoStar, LoopNet) outpacing expense growth, while also disclosing a May 2026 agreement to acquire Zonda for ~$800M cash (expected to close H2 2026) and completion of the Richmond, VA campus expansion.
